To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum power degradation of GaInP/GAs/Ge triple-junction solar cells is almost independent of irradiation particle type and can be predicted by using a unique semi-empirical expression as a function of absorbed NIEL dose".
the maximum power degradation of solar cells can be described by a unique function of the absorbed non-ionizing energy loss (NIEL) dose.
the degradation of solar cells in space is due to displacement damage and that the maximum power degradation is proportional to the absorbed NIEL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the maximum power degradation of solar cells irradiated with electrons or protons.
the development of a new approach for the prediction of the end-of-life performance of solar cells in a space radiation environment.
the development of a methodology that can be applied to the study of any type of solar cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the absorbed NIEL (Nuclear Energy Loss) dose is a very useful quantity in the description of radiation damage to solar cells.
, in the case of the investigated solar cells and the considered radiation environment, the NIEL dose is a very good predictor of the maximum power degradation.
the maximum power degradation is a function of the displacement dose only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a solar cell is a device which can be characterized in terms of NIEL.
the maximum power degradation can be predicted by a unique function, which depends only on the type of solar cell and the absorbed NIEL.
the maximum power degradation can be predicted by using only the absorbed NIEL doses for electrons and protons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, to a first approximation at least, the degradation of the maximum power of GaAs and GaInP solar cells is only dependent on the NIEL absorbed dose.
the maximum power degradation of solar cells can be predicted from NIEL values.
the absorbed NIEL can be used to predict the performance degradation of solar cells irradiated with electrons and proton, which will be useful in the design of space missions.
